endpoints.truth_yaml:
put:
  operationId: updateTimeEntry
  x-verification-status: LIVE-VERIFIED
  x-evidence:
    - PROBE-LOG/20260521-060000-put.workspaces.time-entries-official-live-verified.json
  x-notes: |
    Full-replacement PUT for a time entry. Tool does GET-then-PUT merge with
    an ownership guard (requireCurrentUserEntry) — clockify_entries_update is
    constrained to the API-key owner's own entries. Official spec uses path
    param name 'id'; our spec uses 'timeEntryId' — cosmetic difference, same
    URL path segment. PUT body is built by timeEntryPutPayload: includes
    start (required), end (optional for in-progress), description, projectId,
    taskId, tagIds, billable, type. dry_run mode returns a validated preview
    without hitting upstream. Live probe: entry <redacted-id:1dac181586>
    updated via MCP tool, HTTP 200 returned, changedFields [] (no-op
    same-value update confirms round-trip path is correct). TRUTH entry added
    to /workspaces/{workspaceId}/time-entries/{timeEntryId} path which
    previously had GET and DELETE but no PUT.
  x-truth-iter: iter22
  parameters:
    - {name: workspaceId, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
    - name: timeEntryId
      in: path
      required: true
      description: Time entry ID. Official spec calls this 'id'; our spec uses 'timeEntryId'.
      schema:
        type: string
  requestBody:
    required: true
    content:
      application/json:
        schema:
          type: object
          required: [start]
          properties:
            start: {type: string, description: ISO 8601 datetime}
            end: {type: string, description: ISO 8601 datetime -- omit for in-progress entries}
            description: {type: string, maxLength: 2000}
            projectId: {type: string, nullable: true}
            taskId: {type: string, nullable: true}
            tagIds:
              type: array
              nullable: true
              items:
                type: string
            billable: {type: boolean}
            type: {type: string, enum: [REGULAR, BREAK]}
  responses:
    '200':
      description: Updated time entry object
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            type: object
            description: Same shape as GET /time-entries/{timeEntryId} response
endpoints.notes: Live-verified. PUT /workspaces/{wsId}/time-entries/{entryId} accepted, HTTP 200. Official spec param name is {id}, ours is {timeEntryId} — cosmetic only, no functional discrepancy. TRUTH.openapi.yaml had GET and DELETE for this path but no PUT entry; this iter22 probe adds it. Tool code is correct: entries.go:345 PutWithQuery.

discrepancies.description: Official spec uses path param name 'id'; our spec uses 'timeEntryId'. HTTP path is identical at the positional level. No functional difference.
discrepancies.resolution: No action required. Both specs reference the same endpoint. The param name difference is purely cosmetic in the OpenAPI spec.

discrepancies.description: TRUTH.openapi.yaml at /workspaces/{workspaceId}/time-off/policies/{policyId} currently has only a 'patch:' entry (iter15 LIVE-OVERRIDE). The MCP tool clockify_time_off_policies_update has always used Client.Put (HTTP PUT) since at least commit 5c5e8ca. The iter15 probe mislabeled the HTTP method as PATCH because the comparison was done at the spec level rather than verified at the wire level. This live probe confirms Clockify accepts HTTP PUT at this path.
discrepancies.resolution: Add a PUT entry to TRUTH.openapi.yaml for this path. Update the existing PATCH entry x-notes to clarify: PATCH is used for archive/status toggle (archiveTimeOffPolicy at line 285 uses Client.Patch), while PUT is used for field updates (updateTimeOffPolicy at line 165 uses Client.Put). Both verbs are valid at the same path but serve different operations.

discrepancies.description: Official spec uses path param name 'id'; our spec uses 'policyId'. HTTP path is identical at the positional level.

endpoints.notes: LIVE-VERIFIED. HTTP PUT at /workspaces/{wsId}/time-off/policies/{policyId} returns 200 with full policy object. Key finding: the existing TRUTH.openapi.yaml 'patch:' entry at this path (iter15) incorrectly reflects the update tool's HTTP verb -- the tool has always sent PUT (Client.Put). PATCH at this path is used separately by archiveTimeOffPolicy (status toggle). Both verbs coexist at the same path for different operations. TRUTH.openapi.yaml needs a PUT entry added and the existing PATCH entry x-notes corrected.
